name: Victoria

seo.title: Landscaping in Victoria, BC — Gardens & Tree Care | RNC
seo.description: Garden builds, tree care, irrigation and upkeep for Victoria homes and stratas, planned around the City's tree bylaw and boulevard guidelines.

summary: Victoria lots run from heritage gardens in Rockland and Fairfield to strata courtyards downtown and homes along the Gorge Waterway. Many hold trees the City protects: any tree over 30 cm across, and Garry oak, arbutus, Pacific yew and Pacific dogwood once they pass 50 cm tall.

Boulevards have their own guidelines in the city, and in-ground irrigation is not allowed on them, so sprinkler zones belong on the yard side of the property line. On Gorge and Victoria Arm lots, the first 7 m from the high-water mark stays natural and free of chemical pesticides and fertilizers.

localRules.text: Victoria's Tree Protection Bylaw protects trees on private property with a diameter over 30 cm, and hedges that contain any single stem over 30 cm in diameter. Diameter is measured at breast height, 1.4 m above grade.
localRules.sourceTitle: Property Owners: What You Need to Know About the New Tree Protection Bylaw (City of Victoria info sheet)
localRules.excerpt: A hedge that contains any single stem with a diameter over 30 cm

localRules.text: In Victoria a tree of any size is protected if it grows on a slope steeper than 33 per cent over 10 metres, or within 15 metres of the natural boundary of a watercourse.
localRules.sourceTitle: Property Owners: What You Need to Know About the New Tree Protection Bylaw (City of Victoria info sheet)
localRules.excerpt: A tree of any size that is within 15 metres of the natural boundary of a watercourse

localRules.text: Victoria protects four native species, Garry oak, arbutus, Pacific yew and Pacific dogwood, once they are over 50 cm tall. Even a young oak or arbutus in a bed can need a permit before it is pruned or removed.
localRules.sourceTitle: Property Owners: What You Need to Know About the New Tree Protection Bylaw (City of Victoria info sheet)
localRules.excerpt: Garry Oak (Quercus garryana), Arbutus (Arbutus menziesii), Pacific Yew (Taxus brevifolia) or Pacific Dogwood (Cornus nuttallii) over 50 cm in height measured above natural grade

localRules.text: In Victoria, pruning a protected tree needs a permit only if you cut branches over 10 cm in diameter or remove more than 25% of its live foliage and bud-bearing branches. Lighter pruning to good arboricultural practice needs no permit.
localRules.sourceTitle: Property Owners: What You Need to Know About the New Tree Protection Bylaw (City of Victoria info sheet)
localRules.excerpt: Branches with a diameter >10 cm … More than 25% of the total live foliage and bud bearing branches

localRules.text: If you remove a protected tree in Victoria, you must plant a replacement: one large or medium tree, or two small-species trees. The City holds a refundable deposit until the replacement has survived a year.
localRules.sourceTitle: Property Owners: What You Need to Know About the New Tree Protection Bylaw (City of Victoria info sheet)
localRules.excerpt: If you remove a protected tree, you will be required to replace it.

localRules.text: Victoria's Tree Protection Bylaw applies to trees on private property. You may need a permit to prune or remove a protected tree, or to work in its protected root zone, for example when digging for a patio, wall or irrigation line. Questions go to treepermits@victoria.ca.
localRules.sourceTitle: Tree Protection Bylaw | City of Victoria
localRules.excerpt: If you would like to prune, remove or work in the protected root zone of a bylaw-protected tree, a permit may be required.

localRules.text: Victoria boulevard gardens need no pre-approval, but owners must follow the City's Boulevard Gardening Guidelines, register the garden, and make a BC One Call before digging. Paving over or graveling a boulevard counts as an alteration and is not permitted.
localRules.sourceTitle: Community Gardening: Boulevard Gardens | City of Victoria
localRules.excerpt: Paving over, laying down gravel or similar activities are considered alterations to the boulevard and are not permitted.

localRules.text: Victoria's Boulevard Gardening Guidelines rule out permanent installations such as in-ground irrigation on the boulevard. They also say: dig with hand tools only, contact Parks at least 10 days before digging, keep stones or gravel to 10% of the boulevard, plant no trees, and keep plants under 1 m where sightlines matter (60 cm near intersections and driveways).
localRules.excerpt: Permanent installations such as in-ground irrigation systems and permanent structures and ornaments are not allowed

localRules.text: On Victoria lots along the Gorge Waterway and Victoria Arm, Schedule 2K of the Victoria 2050 OCP keeps a 7 m strip from the high-water mark natural. Removing native trees, shrubs or forest debris there is prohibited, with narrow exceptions. Chemical pesticides and fertilizers must not be used, and fill or seawalls are allowed only where needed to stop erosion.
localRules.sourceTitle: Victoria Arm - Gorge Waterway Design Guidelines, Victoria 2050 OCP Schedule 2K (City of Victoria)
localRules.excerpt: The removal of native trees, shrubs and forest debris within a strip measured 7 metres perpendicular from the high water mark is prohibited

localRules.text: Victoria's Pesticide Use Reduction Bylaw (07-094) bans non-essential pesticide use to maintain trees, shrubs, flowers, ornamental plants and turf on private and public land. Other pesticide use for that purpose needs a City permit. Listed low-risk pesticides and designated invasive species are among the exemptions.
localRules.sourceTitle: Pesticide Use Reduction Bylaw 07-094, consolidated May 22, 2019 (City of Victoria)
localRules.excerpt: A person must not apply or otherwise use pesticides on public land or private land, for the purpose of maintaining outdoor trees, shrubs, flowers, or other ornamental plants

localRules.text: In residential areas, Victoria's Noise Bylaw allows leaf blowers only from 9 am to 8 pm on weekdays and 9 am to 5 pm on weekends and holidays. They must also stay under 65 dBA measured at 15.2 m.
localRules.sourceTitle: Noise Bylaw 03-012, consolidated February 1, 2015 (City of Victoria)
localRules.excerpt: between 9:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. on a weekday, or (ii) between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday

conditions.text: Salt spray is a garden factor near Victoria's shoreline: in a UBC Botanical Garden forum thread, a Victoria gardener living a block from the water reports plants and trees scorched by it every year. Seaside beds there do better with salt-tolerant plants.
conditions.sourceTitle: Oceanfront Plants (UBC Botanical Garden forums, Victoria gardener thread)
conditions.excerpt: plants and trees become fried every year from the salt spray

proof.text: Replanted a James Bay boulevard garden with hand tools only, keeping plants under 60 cm beside the driveway and stones well below a tenth of the strip.

servicesBlurb.grounds-maintenance: Compact city lawns and strata courtyards need regular care, and leaf blowers in Victoria's residential areas may run only within the Noise Bylaw's hours.
servicesBlurb.landscape-installation: New beds and patios on tight Victoria lots have to respect the root zones of trees the City protects, so the layout starts from those trees.
servicesBlurb.irrigation: Victoria boulevards cannot take in-ground irrigation, so systems are laid out to water the yard side of the property line.
servicesBlurb.tree-vegetation: Pruning a protected tree in the city needs a permit only for cuts over 10 cm or more than a quarter of the live foliage, so the scope is settled before work begins.
